# Grid editing has no projection-loss opt-out, and IME is unprobed

## Context

Leaf of #18762, slice 2 (interaction contract). D#17832 OQ2 settled projection loss:
- S2, suspend and reproject, is the default. Delivered by #18764.
- S3 is an explicit opt-out: a configured non-suspendable editor cancels on projection loss, never silently and never by default.
- S4, blocking eviction for non-resumable state, is not adopted. "The IME probe stays owed" before anyone builds it.

Neither the opt-out nor the probe exists. `src/grid/plugin/CellEditing.mjs` has no projection-loss option and no composition handling.

## The Problem

- **The IME probe.** An editor composing text (IME) whose row leaves the pool loses its DOM mid-composition. Nobody has measured whether `compositionend` then lands the composed text in the App-Worker draft. D#17832 made S4 conditional on that measurement.
- **The S3 opt-out.** An application whose editor cannot be suspended has no way to say so.

## The Fix

1. **Probe.** Drive a composition through CDP (`Input.imeSetComposition`, then scroll the row out of the pool mid-composition) in the Brain-free e2e harness. Record whether the composed text reaches the draft. If it does not, file S4 with the measurement.
2. **S3.** Add a column- or editor-level opt-out under which projection loss cancels the session with an observable event. The default stays S2.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The probe's result is pinned by an arm, and the PR states what it means for S4.
- [ ] With the opt-out set, projection loss cancels the session and fires the event. Without it, every S2 arm stays green.

## Out of Scope

- S4 itself, unless the probe proves it necessary (then it is its own leaf).
